column1: # Diet vocabulary (diet-vocabulary/2): what each severe restriction class restricts, derived and measured rather than added by example (staging checkpoint 5, Q5, Q7, Q19).
# class: the class of what a restriction restricts; DietVocabulary.Classes gives its reference type and the default types it feeds (DefaultRestrictionCriteria).

# basis: category = the head term of every food of the frozen USDA catalog (Nom.Api.Tests/Fixtures/Golden/gate-catalog.tsv) in the categories that carry the class, by rule (DietVocabulary.Derive; categories and foods say which and how many gave it; the test checks these rows against the catalog); marker = the term a coating or treatment word of the descriptions gives (battered, sulfured); label = a name an authority lists for the class on labels; translation = the food's name in a language the staged cookbooks are written in (Italian: Artusi's lines; Spanish and French: the food words of the Spanish and French cookery books), staging checkpoint 6, R5.

# decision: in = the pattern is part of the class's default patterns; covered = another pattern of the class already reads the term; out = the term is free of what the class restricts, for the cited reason, and no pattern of the class reads it.
# pattern: the name pattern, read by words (DietPatternRule); "%term %" reads the term only as a whole word, "% term%" only where a word begins.

# Sources: FALCPA = Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act 201(qq) and 403(w) as amended by the Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act of 2004 and the FASTER Act of 2021. FDA-QA5 = FDA, Questions and Answers Regarding Food Allergens, edition 5 (2025). FDA-SESAME = FDA, Voluntary Disclosure of Sesame as an Allergen: Guidance for Industry (2020), the other names under which sesame appears in ingredient statements. FARE = Food Allergy Research and Education, How to Read a Label (the names of each major allergen in ingredient statements), as given in CDC, Voluntary Guidelines for Managing Food Allergies in Schools and Early Care and Education Programs (2013). 21CFR = Title 21, Code of Federal Regulations (139.110 macaroni products: dough of semolina, durum flour or farina; 136.110 bread, rolls and buns: wheat flour; 182.3616 to 182.3862 the sulfiting agents; 101.100(a)(4) sulfites declared at 10 ppm or more). SR = USDA FoodData Central SR Legacy description. CDF = Celiac Disease Foundation, gluten-free grains and flours.
